If we wanted, we could make our diagrams more complex. For example, we could add names as labels for particular objects. Equally, to symbolize the extension of a one-place predicate, we might simply draw a circle around some particular objects and stipulate that the thus encircled objects (and only them) are to fall under the predicate ‘
’, say. To specify multiple predicates we could use colored (or dashed, dotted) lines for arrows and circles.
